findings.category: process/consistency, not a defect in the shipped code
findings.title: The caller-side directory handover was removed from W11b's verification script before W01d landed, diverging from the coordinator's contemporaneous written guidance for the sibling W12 pack to keep an equivalent interim copy
findings.detail: Commit 8bbfaf14a (docs(factory): record the handover question as answered...), already on integ/w00, is authored by the same identity ('archy') 8 minutes before db21ca701, and records: 'This round finishes with the four lines in ReferenceDataGuestDirectory.create in place; when W01d is on integ/w00 the coordinator signals and those four lines are deleted in a small follow-up, so every pack uses one implementation. Until then this pack's copy is the only thing keeping its guests able to write, and removing it early would break every journey.' W12's production file src/factory/reference-data/materials.ts (class ReferenceDataGuestDirectory, verified in the w12-data worktree) still contains chmod(0o755)/chmod(0o770)/podman-unshare-chown today, per that guidance. W11b's second commit (db21ca701) removed the equivalent workaround from its own script, breaking its own ability to produce a live end-to-end proof until W01d lands -- exactly the outcome the coordinator's note warned against for 'every journey'.
findings.mitigatingFactor: This is not a correctness defect and not a misrepresentation: the gate file (B1/B6/B7) is fully transparent that these rows are unchecked and explains why in detail; the coordinator's guidance text was framed around W12's specific production file (ReferenceDataGuestDirectory.create), and W11's own production code (src/factory/reference-image/*.ts) never contained directory-creation/chmod logic in the first place -- only the standalone verification script (scripts/verify-factory-image-pack.ts) did, so nothing shipped in the pack's production surface regressed. No credential, no security control, and no gate integrity is weakened by this choice.
findings.recommendation: The team lead/coordinator should explicitly confirm whether the 'keep an interim copy until W01d lands' policy was meant to bind W11's verification script too. If yes, restore a clearly-marked interim workaround in scripts/verify-factory-image-pack.ts (matching W12's pattern) so B1/B6/B7 can be exercised now rather than blocked until W01d lands. If no (W11's script is disposable tooling and the sibling comparison doesn't apply), record that explicitly in w11b-GATES.md so a future reader does not need to reconstruct this reasoning independently.

findings.title: receipts.json's logDigest for logs/gates.log does not match the file's actual current sha256
findings.detail: receipts.json records logDigest 'sha256:9106502fb57a435b74fea90cdfe7f6f60cc89a7a215c05b8116597c7e43a0538' for /tmp/factory-platform-evidence/w11b/logs/gates.log. Independently computed sha256sum of that file is 'f0a55e3bfe57288df03345949cfa1cc2f6c40ec5929b71ecc3b015eaf2165ec2' -- confirmed with both sha256sum and openssl dgst -sha256, and does not match any obvious truncation of the file's three appended run-blocks either. Every other digest cross-checked (gateFileDigest for tasks/factory/w11b-GATES.md, receiptDigest for logs/journey-mount.json, receiptDigest for logs/publication.json) matched exactly.
findings.mitigatingFactor: The file's mtime (15:36:42.244) and receipts.json's mtime (15:36:42.268) are 24ms apart, consistent with a digest captured a moment before or during a final write rather than deliberate tampering. All of the actual numbers the gate file and receipts.json quote from gates.log (typecheck=0, lint=0, boundaries=0, gate-integrity=0, python 183 cases/100%, new-file/patch PASSED) were independently reproduced by my own reruns and match the log's current content.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the gates.log digest in receipts.json so the evidence chain is auditable byte-for-byte.
